newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears Mannesmann control of Vallourec.
newsitem.headline: EU clears Mannesmann control of Vallourec.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had cleared the acquisition by Mannesmann Roehren Werke (MRW) of a 21-percent stake in France's Vallourec and creation of a seamless tubes venture between the two steel firms.

The Commission said the agreements were likely to increase the companies' combined market share to over 30 percent in a number of areas, including seamless mechanical and powergen tubes, gas cylinders and bearing tubes.
But it took the view that they would face "significant competition" from other producers, notably Italy's Dalmine, Chesterfield Tubes and Desford Tubes of Britain, Germany's Benteler and SKF's Ovako.

"As even on the narrow product and geographic market definitions the operation will not create or strengthen a dominant position the Commission has cleared the notified operation within the first one-month investigation period," the Commission said in a statement.
Mannnesmann AG, which together with Thyssen AG owns MRW, announced the Commission decision to clear the tubes venture earlier on Wednesday.

The agreement, which would make Mannesmann the largest shareholder in France's biggest steel maker effective October 1, has also been approved by the supervisory boards of both companies, and now needs only the approval of Vallourec's annual general meeting, Mannesmann said.
